headline: Shopify puts the first hard numbers on AI-referred orders, and Google says PMax may hand brand searches to Search
intro: A quiet day on the platform changelogs, but Shopify's Q3 call gave the first measured read on what agent traffic does at checkout and Google's PMax help page now says brand queries may be routed away from PMax.

items.title: Shopify Q3 call: orders from AI searches up 3.3x, AI-referred sessions convert 64% more often than organic search
items.source: PPC Land, reporting Shopify's Q3 2026 earnings call
items.what: On its Q3 call on 3 Nov Shopify gave the first measured read on agent-driven commerce across its merchant base, per PPC Land's write-up. Orders from AI searches rose 3.3x year on year, from a base Shopify called small and did not quantify. AI traffic to merchant storefronts rose 2.6x. AI-referred sessions converted 64% more often than organic search, and searches powered by Shopify Catalog converted at twice the rate of general AI search. 74% of AI-attributed purchases came from categories outside the top 100, the long tail. Shop Pay is now usable inside Claude, Instinct and Grok for any merchant. Shopify attributed the figures to its global search API usage and said volume is still small.
items.sowhat: This is the benchmark a client will hold feed work to: AI-referred sessions that convert better than organic, and Catalog-structured data converting at twice the rate of unstructured. The 74% long-tail figure argues for keyword and attribute depth across the whole range, not just hero lines. YuMOVE's master feed comes out of Shopify, so check its Catalog eligibility and whether its Shop Pay agent checkout is live before the holiday peak. Treat the multiples as directional: the base is small and Shopify said so.

items.title: Google: PMax may now filter out brand and navigational queries and serve them through dedicated Search campaigns
items.source: Search Engine Roundtable, confirmed on Google's Ads help page
items.what: Google added a new exception to its help page on how Performance Max interacts with other campaigns. It now reads: Performance Max campaigns may also filter out navigational or brand-specific search queries to prioritize serving them through dedicated Search campaigns, so brand-related queries are handled by campaigns offering more precise control. Google's advice: make sure dedicated brand Search campaigns have sufficient budget and eligible ads, and consider adding Search Themes to the PMax campaign. Spotted by Hana Kobzova of PPC News Feed and reported by Barry Schwartz on 3 Nov. The page carries no date and does not say whether feed-based or Shopping-only PMax is treated differently.
items.sowhat: Every Google Shopping feed we run sits behind PMax for most clients, so a share of brand-term volume and its revenue may move out of the feed campaigns and into brand Search before Black Friday. The ROAS module reads trailing windows, so watch for a step down in PMax revenue with a matching step up in brand Search rather than a real loss. Raise it with each client's PPC agency this week: brand Search budgets, eligible ads and PMax Search Themes are their levers, not ours, but a PMax read that drops for this reason must not be read as a feed problem.

items.title: Mastercard discloses an agentic commerce partnership with OpenAI on its Q3 call; Shop Pay already runs on Agent Pay
items.source: The Paypers, reporting Mastercard's Q3 2026 earnings call
items.what: On its Q3 call Mastercard said it has partnered with OpenAI across Agent Pay, payments, services and AI transformation, per The Paypers. CEO Michael Miebach called agentic commerce early days: volumes are limited but rising week on week, and the holiday season is expected to accelerate them. The Agent Pay stack is Agent Pay itself, Verifiable Intent, Agentic Trust Intelligence and Agent Connect. Mastercard said Shopify's Shop Pay uses Agent Pay with network tokens on multiple agentic platforms, and that it backs full tokenisation for agent purchases rather than one-time virtual card numbers. No primary Mastercard release was published; the detail is from the call.
items.sowhat: The payment rail for agent purchases is standardising around network tokens, with Shopify's Shop Pay already running on it and OpenAI now partnered. Nothing for a feed team to do this week, but it is the line that explains to a client why Instant Checkout in ChatGPT is a matter of when, not if, and why the feed and Catalog data behind it needs to be ready first. A QBR slide, not a brief.

items.title: Microsoft Clarity: checkout appears in 25% of AI-agent sessions against 15% of human sessions, across 5.2 million sessions
items.source: PPC Land, on Microsoft Clarity's agent activity report
items.what: Microsoft Clarity published What AI Agents Do on Websites, a read of 5.2 million sessions, alongside the general release of its Agent Activity Dashboard on 29 Oct. Checkout events appeared in 25.21% of agentic sessions against 14.65% of human sessions. The agents measured come from the agentic browsers of OpenAI, Google and Anthropic. Clarity's own caveat: agent sessions cluster on retail and travel sites, which inflates the checkout share against an all-site human baseline. Figures are Clarity's; no other analytics vendor has published a comparable read yet.
items.sowhat: Pairs with the HUMAN Security read on Muse traffic carried on 2 Nov: agent sessions are showing up in client analytics as unusually checkout-heavy, low-browse visits. If a client's PPC agency or analytics team reports a conversion-rate shift with no campaign change behind it, agent traffic is one cause to rule in. Worth a line in the next Reiss and Superdry reviews, the two accounts with US markets where these agentic browsers launched first. Vendor data, so quote it as Clarity's finding, not an industry figure.
